docs.title: About this book
docs.text:
De motu cordis (1628), the short Latin book in which William Harvey overturned the teaching of Galen: from the movements of the heart and arteries seen in living animals, the valves of the veins and the quantity of blood the heart sends out, he shows that the blood circulates. In the English of Robert Willis, from the Sydenham Society's Works of William Harvey (1847).

From Wikisource · Public domain

William Harvey (1578–1657), Exercitatio anatomica de motu cordis et sanguinis in animalibus (Latin), 1628; translated by Robert Willis (1799–1878), The Works of William Harvey, Sydenham Society, 1847; text from Wikisource. This book is not stored in this library: each chapter is read from Wikisource when it is opened, shown in this library's format, and ends with its own attribution. Licence: Public domain.
